quebec-city.overview: Quebec City and Montreal feature accessible day hikes through forested hills and glacial valleys just outside the urban centers. Near Quebec City, Parc national de la Jacques-Cartier provides steep climbs like the Les Loups trail, rewarding hikers with sweeping views of a deep river valley. Montreal's Mount Royal features easy, graded paths right in the city. The most popular hiking season aligns with the vibrant fall foliage.

queenstown.overview: Queenstown is the most popular base for exploring New Zealand's Southern Alps on foot, offering everything from steep day hikes to multi-day alpine routes. The long, steep hike up Ben Lomond begins with a gondola ride to skip the lower slopes, rewarding hikers with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the surrounding peaks. Trekkers come for the Routeburn Track, a 20-mile alpine crossing, and the Kepler Track, both requiring advance hut bookings. The best conditions run from December through March, when the high passes are clear of snow.

rajaampat.overview: Raja Ampat is most famous for its underwater landscapes, but the islands do have some worthwhile short walks. The best known are the wooden stairs to the karst viewpoint at Piaynemo and the steeper rock scramble to the view at Wayag. Short jungle trails on Waigeo lead to bird viewing areas. Access to most trailheads is by boat.

redwood.overview: Redwood National and State Parks have day hiking through ancient old-growth forests and along rugged Pacific coastlines. The signature routes wind beneath towering canopies, like the easy stroll from Gold Bluffs Beach through Fern Canyon, a slot canyon carpeted with delicate maiden hair ferns, or the 12-mile loop trail that connects the canyon to the Prairie Creek visitor center inland. Summers can be foggy and winters are rainy; spring and fall have the highest odds of clear skies.

months.6: Dry, mild weather arrives. Coastal fog can linger over the groves into the morning, but the forest loops and coastal trails are highly accessible, though Fern Canyon requires a parking reservation.
months.7: Summer fog often hangs over the coast and groves, keeping the air cool, but the trails are dry. The ten-mile James Irvine Trail provides a permit-free route to the coast.
months.8: Late summer keeps the trails dry, though fog often blankets the coast and groves. Hikers can explore the towering groves and coastal bluffs, with Fern Canyon parking still requiring a reservation.

rioja.overview: Rioja has modest but scenic walking, blending agricultural landscapes with the rugged backdrop of the Sierra de Cantabria. Most routes are easy to moderate day hikes that start directly from the wine towns, leading through rolling vineyards and along the Ebro River. The best walking is in spring and autumn, avoiding the intense summer heat and cold winters.

rivieramaya.overview: The Riviera Maya's walking is flat and easy: jungle paths and coastal trails. The best are short nature trails around cenotes and the shaded forest paths linking the ancient ruins at Coba.

rwanda.overview: Hiking in Rwanda includes steep, muddy volcano climbs and dense forest trails that require a park guide. In Volcanoes National Park, hikers climb Mount Bisoke or Mount Karisimbi, or take the jungle trail to Dian Fossey's grave. Further south, Nyungwe National Park provides a network of trails through ancient montane rainforest.

santorini.overview: Santorini's best-known hike is the famous caldera-rim path from Fira to Oia, a hilly route that traces the edge of the volcanic crater. Hikers earn views of the Aegean Sea and the island's whitewashed villages that cannot be seen from the road. Beyond the rim, the island features modest coastal walks and paths through dry, terraced hills.

sardinia.overview: Sardinia features rugged Mediterranean hiking, from the deep limestone canyons of the Supramonte to the high peaks of the Gennargentu. Steep trails lead through wild macchia and ancient oak forests down to isolated coves like Cala Goloritzé. Spring and autumn provide the best weather for exploring the island's dramatic coastal cliffs and mountainous interior.

scottish-highlands-skye.overview: The Scottish Highlands and the Isle of Skye offer some of the most dramatic hiking landscapes in the UK, defined by deep glens, rugged coastlines, and jagged peaks. Iconic routes include the Quiraing landslip and the Old Man of Storr, where steep, rocky paths lead to sweeping views of the sea and moors. Multi-day hikers can tackle the 96-mile West Highland Way through the mainland valleys. The best conditions run from May to September, though the middle of the year brings notorious biting midges.

sicily.overview: Sicily offers a mix of volcanic landscapes and coastal trails. The main draw is Mount Etna, where hikers can explore lower craters independently or hire a guide to reach the active summit zone when conditions allow. Elsewhere, the Zingaro Nature Reserve provides coastal paths above the Mediterranean, and the Madonie mountains have forested ridges. Spring and fall are the best times to walk, avoiding the intense summer heat.

singapore.overview: Singapore has modest but accessible walking, primarily on paved paths and elevated walkways. One popular route is the Southern Ridges, an easy trail connecting Mount Faber to Kent Ridge Park via the striking Henderson Waves bridge. Heat and humidity are constant year-round.

srilanka.overview: Sri Lanka's hiking includes lush hill country trails and striking rock fortress climbs. The most famous route is the night ascent of Adam's Peak, a steep climb up thousands of stairs to catch the sunrise, while day hikers head to the viewpoints of Ella Rock and Pidurangala. The best hiking aligns with the drier months from December to March.

svalbard.overview: Hiking in Svalbard means guided day walks across open tundra and glaciers, often reached by boat from Longyearbyen. Because of polar bears, anyone leaving the settlement must carry a means of scaring them off, and most hikers go with an armed guide. The short summer window offers stark Arctic scenery, with routes tracing remote shorelines or climbing up local peaks like Sarkofagen.

rajasthan-golden-triangle.overview: Rajasthan has more hiking than its cities suggest. Guided treks cross Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary, trails at Mount Abu climb to 1,722-meter Guru Shikhar, and Jaipur's Nahargarh Fort has a hill path. Dust haze builds before the monsoon, and smog settles in from November.

months.1: Cool, dry days suit the Aravalli trails near Kumbhalgarh and the climb to Guru Shikhar at Mount Abu, though winter smog can haze the plains.
months.2: Cool mornings and mild afternoons make this a prime month for the Kumbhalgarh treks and the forest trails at Mount Abu.
months.3: Heat builds quickly. Start at dawn for the Kumbhalgarh ridges, the Mount Abu trails or the path up to Nahargarh Fort.
months.4: Intense heat and pre-monsoon dust storms leave the air hazy and the hillsides unpleasant for hiking. Only a short dawn outing is advisable.
months.5: Brutal heat and dust-laden air make hiking on the exposed hillsides dangerous.
months.6: Extreme heat and dusty haze linger until the monsoon arrives, and the exposed hillsides are unsafe for hiking.
months.7: Heavy monsoon rain turns the trails to mud and brings high humidity. The Aravalli hills turn green, but Mount Abu's summit paths can be foggy and slippery.
months.8: The rains continue, keeping trails muddy and slippery. The hills are green, but hiking remains difficult.
months.9: The monsoon tapers off, but humidity stays high and trails are still recovering from the rains.
months.10: The rains end and the hills are briefly green. Trails dry out, making morning hikes at Kumbhalgarh and Mount Abu viable again.
months.11: Temperatures drop to comfortable levels and the Kumbhalgarh and Mount Abu trails open up, though smog can start to build over the plains.
months.12: Cool, dry days are good for treks at Kumbhalgarh and the Guru Shikhar climb, though winter smog often hazes the plains.

san-miguel-guanajuato.overview: The best hiking here is in the Sierra de Santa Rosa above Guanajuato, where trails climb through oak and arbutus forest past Peralillo Dam. Near San Miguel, the botanical garden at El Charco del Ingenio has easy paths through cactus scrub.

months.1: Dry, mild winter days suit the oak-forest loop in the Sierra de Santa Rosa and the easy paths of El Charco del Ingenio.
months.2: Clear skies and comfortable temperatures continue, with good footing on the Santa Rosa trails above Guanajuato.
months.3: Temperatures rise. Start early on the Santa Rosa trails, since the unshaded stretches get hot by midday.
months.4: Warm, dry conditions dominate. The Santa Rosa oak forest gives some shade, but carry plenty of water and start early.
months.5: The warmest time of year. Dusty paths and midday heat call for early starts, ideally in the shaded forest of the Sierra de Santa Rosa.
months.6: Summer rains begin and occasionally muddy the paths. Mornings usually stay clear for a hike.
months.7: Frequent afternoon downpours make the steep dirt trails slippery. Stick to morning outings or the garden at El Charco del Ingenio.
months.8: The rainy season continues with regular afternoon showers. The sierra is greener, but trails can be muddy.
months.9: Showers taper off and the hillsides stay green, with clear, fresh air for morning hikes in the sierra.
months.10: The rains end, leaving clear skies and comfortable temperatures for the Santa Rosa trails.
months.11: Mild, dry weather returns completely, with reliable conditions on the Santa Rosa loop and around San Miguel.
months.12: Cool, dry winter days are ideal for the climb through the Sierra de Santa Rosa above Guanajuato.

rio.overview: Rio de Janeiro has rugged day hikes within the city limits, climbing through Atlantic Forest to viewpoints over the beaches and bays. The trails are steep and often involve scrambling, and a guide is advised for the exposed rock section of Pedra da Gávea. Dois Irmãos and Pico da Tijuca are shorter steep climbs. On the far western edge, Pedra do Telégrafo above Barra de Guaratiba is a popular half-day climb.
